title: Pipe selection and camera_focus_pair never clear app.pullback — contradicts the 'any selection ends it' contract
evidence: camera_set_selection doc (main.odin:1512): "nothing selected returns to the bird's-eye fit. Any selection change ends an in-flight pullback (the player's nav owns the camera)." Node branch (1521-1523): app.cam_zoom_to = 2.3 / app.pullback = false / return. Pipe branch (1535-1538): app.cam_wx_to = (ax + bx) / 2 / app.cam_wy_to = (ay + by) / 2 / app.cam_zoom_to = 2.6 / return — no pullback write. camera_focus_pair (1559-1562): app.cam_wx_to = (ax + bx) / 2 / app.cam_wy_to = (ay + by) / 2 / app.cam_zoom_to = 2.6 / } — no pullback write.
detail: Selecting a pipe (QoS panel) or a crisis-banner/SLA focus during a pullback leaves pullback=true, so camera_update eases to the new focus at the 0.05 pullback rate (~1.5-2s) instead of 0.14 (~0.5s). Deviates from the comment and PR claim 'any user camera input yields the pullback instantly'.
recommended_fix: Add app.pullback = false next to the app.cam_zoom_to = 2.6 writes in camera_set_selection's pipe branch and in camera_focus_pair.

title: The fit min() expression is triplicated despite camera_fit's 'ONE source' comment
evidence: camera_update (main.odin:1595): fit := min(f32(v.win_w)/v.world_w, f32(v.win_h)/v.world_h). camera_fit (main.odin:1674-1676): "// camera_fit — the current camera-fit scale (min of the window/world ratios; // the same derivation view_compute + camera_update use — ONE source)." camera_fit body: return min(f32(v.win_w)/v.world_w, f32(v.win_h)/v.world_h). view_compute (view.odin:401-404): sx := f32(win_w) / v.world_w / sy := f32(win_h) / v.world_h / v.scale = min(sx, sy).
detail: The comment claims ONE source but the same expression is copy-pasted in three places; a future fit-derivation change (e.g. aspect handling) must be synchronized in all three or views diverge silently.
recommended_fix: Make camera_update call camera_fit(v) (the two main.odin copies collapse), and ideally have render export a fit helper view_compute reuses.

title: pullback_feed re-implements spawn_fx_feed's NODE_SPAWNED id walk-back instead of sharing it
evidence: pullback_feed (main.odin:1634-1640): "// newest-first walk-back (the spawn_fx precedent): the LAST spawn event // in the slice is the newest node (next_node_id-1)..." remaining := n_spawns / for e in events { / if e.tag != pp.EVENT_TAG_NODE_SPAWNED { / continue. spawn_fx.odin:132-139: "// newest-first walk-back: the LAST spawn event in the slice is the newest // node (next_node_id-1); earlier ones walk back through the ids." remaining := n_spawns / for e in events { / if e.tag != pp.EVENT_TAG_NODE_SPAWNED { / continue / id := topo.next_node_id - remaining.
detail: Two independent copies of the zero-payload spawn-event→node-id derivation; any change to event ordering or allocation semantics must be fixed in both. The copies are behaviorally identical today.
recommended_fix: Extract one shared helper (e.g. in app/render near spawn_fx) mapping a NODE_SPAWNED event slice to node ids, and call it from both feeds.

title: New camera/pullback tests skip the catalogs_destroy cleanup the package's own fixture precedent uses
evidence: camera_input_test.odin:60: ictx.view = new(rnd.View). Defers (78-80): defer destroy(&ictx) / defer pp.run_destroy(&st) / defer delete(log) — no catalogs_destroy. pullback_test.odin:30: append(&app.cat.node_types, — defer only pp.run_destroy(&app.state). exec_test.odin:53-55 (the fixture precedent): wire_test_cat(cat) / defer pp.catalogs_destroy(cat).
detail: wire_test_cat appends pipe_tiers/node_types and the View is heap-allocated; neither is freed, unlike exec_test's identical fixture. Leaks under tracking-allocator runs (ODN-18 discipline).
recommended_fix: Add defer pp.catalogs_destroy(&cat_storage) to each camera_input_test proc and free (or stack-allocate) the new'd View; free app.cat in pullback_test.

title: Fractional wheel deltas below 1.0 per frame truncate to a silent no-op — no cross-frame accumulator
evidence: camera_zoom_step :: proc(z, delta: f32) -> f32 { / f := f32(1) / for d := i32(delta); d > 0; d -= 1 { / f *= CAM_ZOOM_STEP / } / for d := i32(delta); d < 0; d += 1 { / f /= CAM_ZOOM_STEP / }.
detail: A gentle trackpad scroll delivering per-frame |delta| < 1.0 truncates to zero notches and never zooms; the PR's 'fractional deltas ... fire whole notches' holds only when raylib batches ≥1.0 per frame. Same truncation as the old NOC scroll, but zoom is now a primary input.
recommended_fix: Accumulate fractional wheel delta in Input (carry the remainder across frames) and fire whole notches when it crosses ±1.
